correctness.rationale: The finite-length conditional-entropy identity follows from Markov shielding and independent first-wave assignment; its thermodynamic series converges absolutely. A positive geometric mutual-information expansion gives a strictly convex objective and a unique minimizer. Under \(p=t\sqrt\delta\), two geometric flank distances yield the locally uniform limit \(t\log2+1/(2t)\); the entropy expansion has an \(o(\sqrt\delta)\) expected remainder and a Gamma–uniform decomposition determines the coefficient. Convex argmin convergence yields the sharp minimizer and minimum, and dominated convergence gives the equal-batch constant. A checker independently matches 125 finite distributions within \(4.44\times10^{-15}\), supporting finite formula consistency but not replacing the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Under the two-round budget, equal-sized waves have positive limiting path-KL loss per site as the binary Markov chain approaches perfect order. Tuning the first-wave anchors on the scale \(\xi^{-1/2}\) makes that loss vanish at the sharp rate \(\sqrt{2\log2/\xi}\), producing an unbounded \(\sqrt\xi\) relative advantage. This addresses a physically motivated finite-budget optimization boundary beyond the existing many-round geodesic approximation.
